note: The two market-wide inputs of the cost of capital, as their publishers served them on the day they were fetched. src/calculator.py reads both through this manifest and refuses a file whose bytes no longer hash to what is recorded here. Neither is revised after publication in the rows this reads: a daily Treasury yield is an observed market price, and the implied equity risk premium for a month is computed once, at the start of that month, and left in place.

risk_free_rate.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity, Quoted on an Investment Basis, percent, daily
risk_free_rate.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), read through FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
risk_free_rate.licence: a public-domain series of the United States government
risk_free_rate.rule: the value on the last date on or before the cutoff that carries a number; FRED writes '.' on a day with no observation, and that day is skipped rather than read as zero

equity_risk_premium.series: Implied ERP by month, September 2008 to current
equity_risk_premium.publisher: Aswath Damodaran, Stern School of Business, New York University
equity_risk_premium.column: the trailing-twelve-month premium with sustainable payout, found by its header ending in 'with sustainable payout'
equity_risk_premium.why_this_column: it is the first of the five premiums Damodaran's own home page lists for each month -- 'Implied ERP on September 1, 2026 = 4.14% (Trailing 12 month, with adjusted payout); 4.09% (Trailing 12 month cash yield); ...' -- and the one his cost-of-capital updates carry
equity_risk_premium.rule: the row whose start-of-month date is strictly before the cutoff. The workbook carries no publication date; each month's premium is computed on the first of the month and posted in its first days, so a cutoff on the first of a month reads the month before rather than a number that may not yet have been posted
